caveat:
"First contact" is a European frame. These years record when Europeans arrived and wrote it
down; the peoples already living here had their own long histories of these encounters, and of
the places and routes Europeans then claimed to have discovered. Contact also usually arrived
before Europeans did: trade goods, horses and above all epidemic disease moved along Indigenous
networks decades ahead of any European traveller — the smallpox epidemic of 1780–82 reached the
northern Plains through Indigenous trade and warfare routes and killed a large share of the
population in country no European had yet visited. The dates are uneven in kind as well: some
mark a ship passing offshore, others a wintering or a permanent post, and in the far north and
the deep interior they are the best documented guess rather than a record of what happened first.

regions.name: Pacific coastal basin
regions.event: Mackenzie reaches salt water at Bella Coola, 22 July 1793

regions.name: Fraser and Lower Mainland
regions.event: Simon Fraser descends the river to the Strait of Georgia, May–July 1808

regions.name: Okanagan and Similkameen
regions.event: David Stuart travels north from Fort Okanogan into the Okanagan, 1811; Fort Kamloops 1812

regions.name: Columbia and Kootenay
regions.event: David Thompson crosses Howse Pass and builds Kootenae House on the upper Columbia, 1807

regions.name: Yukon basin
regions.event: Robert Campbell descends the Pelly, 1843; Fort Selkirk 1848

regions.name: Peace and Athabasca
regions.event: Peter Pond crosses Methye Portage and winters on the Athabasca, 1778–79

regions.name: Lower Mackenzie
regions.event: Fort Good Hope, 1805; Fort Norman and Great Bear, 1810

regions.name: Arctic coast and islands
regions.event: The Canadian Arctic Expedition, 1913–18, and the police posts of the 1900s–20s
regions.note: A deliberate backstop for the parts of the archipelago nothing more specific covers. Every island entry below improves it.

regions.name: Canadian Missouri (Milk River)
regions.event: Peter Fidler winters with the Piikani, 1792–93 — the nearest documented presence
regions.note: The weakest entry in this file. No documented European presence in the Canadian Missouri basin before the 19th century was found; Fidler was probably north of it. Needs a specialist source.

regions.name: North Saskatchewan
regions.event: Anthony Henday's journey of 1754–55, the first European in what is now Alberta

regions.name: South Saskatchewan
regions.event: David Thompson winters with the Piikani on the Bow, 1787–88
regions.note: Both candidate anchors (Thompson 1787, Fidler 1792) are winters spent with the Piikani, so contact plainly predated them through Cree and Assiniboine middlemen and the French posts on the lower Saskatchewan.

regions.name: Assiniboine and Red
regions.event: La Vérendrye builds Fort Rouge and Fort La Reine, October 1738

regions.name: Winnipeg River and Rainy Lake
regions.event: Fort Saint-Pierre on Rainy Lake, 1731
regions.note: Jacques de Noyon is said to have wintered on Rainy Lake in 1688, but the account is a late second-hand deposition, so the documented post of 1731 is used instead.

regions.name: Lower Saskatchewan and Nelson
regions.event: Henry Kelsey travels inland from York Factory, 1690–92

regions.name: Churchill River basin
regions.event: Frobisher at Frog Portage, 1774; Île-à-la-Crosse, 1776

regions.name: Keewatin and southern Baffin
regions.event: J. B. Tyrrell descends the Dubawnt and Kazan, 1893–94, and meets the Ahiarmiut

regions.name: Northern Ontario
regions.event: Henley House, 1743, the first inland post; Osnaburgh, 1786
regions.note: Thin. Henley House is a post, not a contact: traders and Indigenous middlemen moved through this country from the 1670s and the true date is almost certainly earlier.

regions.name: Northern Quebec
regions.event: HBC inland posts of the 1830s; A. P. Low's surveys, 1890s

regions.name: Great Lakes basin
regions.event: Dollier and Galinée winter at Long Point, 1669–70

regions.name: Ottawa valley
regions.event: Champlain ascends the Ottawa to Allumette Island, 1613

regions.name: St. Lawrence basin
regions.event: Jean de Quen reaches Lac Saint-Jean, 1647; the Chicoutimi post, 1676
regions.note: The basin's interior, not its river: Cartier's 1535 voyage is the corridor entry below. The 1647 date for the Saguenay interior is universally repeated but was not checked against the Dictionary of Canadian Biography in the pass that produced this file.

regions.name: North Shore and Gaspé
regions.event: Cartier's first voyage coasts the Gulf's north shore and raises a cross at Gaspé, July 1534

regions.name: Saint John and St. Croix
regions.event: de Monts and Champlain at Île Sainte-Croix, 26 June 1604; the Saint John named that month

regions.name: Maritime coastal
regions.event: The Acadian coast of the de Monts expedition, 1604–05

regions.name: Newfoundland and Labrador interior
regions.event: A. P. Low's Geological Survey traverse of the Labrador peninsula, 1893–95

regions.name: L'Anse aux Meadows
regions.event: The Norse outpost at L'Anse aux Meadows, radiocarbon 990–1050, one felling dated to 1021
regions.note: A different kind of fact from everything else here: a single short-lived outpost with no continuity to what came after. It is why the timeline offers 1000 as a start date.

regions.name: Newfoundland
regions.event: Cabot's landfall, 24 June 1497; the Dictionary of Canadian Biography is explicit that the site is not established

regions.name: Strait of Belle Isle
regions.event: Basque whaling at Red Bay from the 1530s, worked for some seventy years

regions.name: Prince Edward Island
regions.event: Cartier coasts the island, July 1534

regions.name: The St. Lawrence to Hochelaga
regions.event: Cartier winters at Stadacona and reaches Hochelaga, 2 October 1535
regions.note: The river itself, which was the route; the basin entry above carries the interior.

regions.name: Huronia and Georgian Bay
regions.event: Champlain reaches the Wendat by the French River, 1615

regions.name: Sault Ste. Marie and Lake Superior
regions.event: Jogues and Raymbault at the Sault, 1641; Radisson and Des Groseilliers winter on Superior, 1659–60

regions.name: James Bay shore
regions.event: Hudson reaches James Bay, 1 November 1610, and winters there

regions.name: The Hudson Bay lowland shore
regions.event: Hudson's voyage of 1610–11 along the bay's southern shore

regions.name: The bay's west shore
regions.event: Hudson's voyage of 1610–11; Button winters at the Nelson in 1612

regions.name: The Kivalliq shore
regions.event: Button coasts north from the Nelson, 1612–13; Munk 1619; Foxe 1631

regions.name: The bay's east shore
regions.event: Hudson's voyage of 1610–11 down the bay's eastern shore

regions.name: The James Bay factories
regions.event: Charles Fort, 1668; Moose Factory, 1673; Fort Albany, 1679

regions.name: The Nelson's mouth
regions.event: Thomas Button winters at the Nelson, 1612–13

regions.name: Churchill
regions.event: The post at Churchill, 1717; Prince of Wales Fort from 1731

regions.name: Nunavik's Hudson coast
regions.event: Richmond Fort, 1749; Great Whale River, 1820

regions.name: Ungava Bay and the Koksoak
regions.event: Kohlmeister and Kmoch, guided by Inuit, reach a camp on the Koksoak, 25 August 1811

regions.name: Lake Melville and the south Labrador coast
regions.event: French then HBC posts at North West River and Rigolet

regions.name: The Moravian coast
regions.event: Jens Haven founds the mission at Nain, August 1771; Okak 1776, Hopedale 1782

regions.name: Southern Baffin Island
regions.event: Frobisher enters Frobisher Bay, 1576; three voyages, 1576–78

regions.name: Cumberland Sound
regions.event: William Penny, guided by Eenoolooapik, re-enters Cumberland Sound, 1840

regions.name: Repulse Bay and Committee Bay
regions.event: Rae winters at Fort Hope, 1846–47, and surveys Committee Bay the next spring

regions.name: Boothia and the Netsilik
regions.event: John Ross's Victory winters at Felix Harbour, 1829–33, four winters among the Netsilik

regions.name: King William Island
regions.event: Amundsen winters at Gjoa Haven, 1903–05

regions.name: The Coronation Gulf coast
regions.event: Franklin's first expedition charts the coast east from the Coppermine, summer 1821

regions.name: The Beaufort coast
regions.event: Franklin's second expedition, July 1826: Franklin west and Richardson east from the delta

regions.name: Herschel Island
regions.event: American whalers winter at Pauline Cove, 1890–91

regions.name: The Parry Channel islands
regions.event: Parry through Lancaster Sound; winters at Winter Harbour, Melville Island, 1819–20

regions.name: Banks Island
regions.event: McClure's Investigator, 1850–53, at Mercy Bay

regions.name: Victoria Island
regions.event: Collinson explores Prince Albert Sound, 1851–53
regions.note: A genuine judgement: Dease and Simpson sighted the south shore in 1838–39, and Stefansson's sustained contact with the Inuinnait was 1910.

regions.name: Ellesmere Island
regions.event: The Nares expedition winters in the Hall Basin, 1875–76; Fort Conger, 1881

regions.name: The Sverdrup Islands
regions.event: Sverdrup's second Fram expedition, 1898–1902, maps some 260,000 km²

regions.name: Haida Gwaii
regions.event: Juan Pérez reaches Haida Gwaii, 18–19 July 1774, and trades with Haida from canoes

regions.name: Vancouver Island
regions.event: Cook anchors at Yuquot in Nootka Sound, 29 March – 26 April 1778

regions.name: The Strait of Georgia and the inner channels
regions.event: Vancouver's survey of 1792–94

regions.name: New Caledonia
regions.event: Fort McLeod, 1805; Fort St James and Fort Fraser, 1806; Fort George, 1807

regions.name: Great Slave Lake
regions.event: Hearne crosses the lake, December 1771 – January 1772; Fort Resolution, 1786

regions.name: The Coppermine's mouth
regions.event: Hearne reaches the Arctic Ocean at Bloody Falls, 15 July 1771

regions.name: The Mackenzie delta
regions.event: Mackenzie reaches the Arctic Ocean, 13 July 1789, meeting Inuvialuit in the delta

regions.name: Fort Chipewyan and the Peace
regions.event: Fort Chipewyan, 1788; Boyer's post at the site of Fort Vermilion the same year
